summary: Ferry County lookout site on Colville NF: rag camp 1922, 30-foot L-4 tower 1944, last lookout removed 1970; register says footings and a guy anchor remain.

facts.design: 30-foot tower with L-4 cab (1944); the 1926 tower was a 30-foot pole tower with a 6-by-6-foot cab
facts.status_note: Last lookout removed in 1970; the register says a guy line anchor and the last tower's footings are all that remain
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Colville National Forest

access.note: Sources describe a route up Forest Road 6120 on National Forest land and do not say it is gated or closed. No tower remains.

visit.trail_note: Hiking distance zero to 1.5 miles; 4WD clearance needed for the last stretch, per WillhiteWeb

events.note: Rag camp with a 20-foot pole platform; start of the site
Tower completed by July 1, 1923, per a 1923 entry quoted on the Weebly page
Glass-enclosed cab added by Hougland; Willhite dates it 1927, the passage quoted on the Weebly page is dated February 1928
Clarence Stovik listed as lookout; Willhite also lists him for 1931 to 1933
Stovik sighted a smoke on Big Goosmus Creek on June 23; a landowner had set it while getting rid of slash without a permit
Construction started on a cabin for the lookout's use, per the Republic News-Miner quoted on the Weebly page and Willhite
Aircraft Warning Service use, activated August 3, 1942; sleeping quarters added with AWS funds
30-foot tower with L-4 cab built in 1944, replacing the 1926 tower
Mrs. Mabel Newton and her daughter from Curlew stationed there
Leonard Wang listed as lookout; the last name in these sources
Last lookout removed; firelookout.com says destroyed
1942 outhouse burned in the Stickpin Fire; the lookout itself was already gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: WillhiteWeb gives 1927 for Hougland's glass-enclosed cab; the Weebly page quotes a passage dated February 1928. The story reports both.
The register and WillhiteWeb say removed in 1970; firelookout.com says destroyed. The story reports both words.
The register gives 5,864 ft (1,787 m), which matches the brief's 1787.3 m; WillhiteWeb gives a lookout elevation of 5,978 ft. Elevation is not used in the story.

notes_for_editor: Brief's elevation and register coordinates match, so no correction. Staffing entries are list names and years, not full tenures. The 2019 photo caption is the latest dated observation; no source describes the site after 2019. The California pages titled Marble Mountain are a different lookout and were not used. No photos added; the register cites photos credited to Rex Kamstra and Rod Fosback, but I did not capture image URLs.
